records.source: וַיְהִ֣י אַבְרָ֔ם בֶּן־תִּשְׁעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְתֵ֣שַׁע שָׁנִ֑ים וַיֵּרָ֨א יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֲנִי־אֵ֣ל שַׁדַּ֔י הִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ לְפָנַ֖י וֶהְיֵ֥ה תָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And was Abram a son of ninety years and nine years, and appeared YHWH to Abram and said to him, I [am] God Almighty; walk before me and be blameless.
pieces: When Abram was ninety-nine, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty. Live your life before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and be wholehearted,

L.1: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Abram and said to him, "I am God Almighty; walk before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and be blameless,

R.1: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to him again. He said, "I am God Almighty. Live in a way that pleases {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and be honest and good in everything you do.

decisions.choice: God Almighty (El Shaddai): a divine name of uncertain meaning
decisions.reason: El Shaddai is a name used in Genesis for God as the giver of the promises (28:3; 35:11), and Exodus 6:3 says the patriarchs knew God by it. Its exact meaning is uncertain. "Almighty" follows the old translations; others link it to a word for mountain or explain it as "the one who is sufficient".

decisions.choice: walk before me and be blameless: live in my presence with integrity
decisions.reason: "Walk before" means to live in someone's sight, serving them. "Blameless" is the word used of Noah (6:9): whole, of complete integrity.

decisions.choice: ninety-nine years: thirteen years after Ishmael
decisions.reason: Abram was eighty-six when Ishmael was born (16:16). Thirteen years have passed with no word recorded from God.

records.heading: Circumcision, the sign of the covenant

records.source: וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה בְרִיתִ֖י בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְאַרְבֶּ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ בִּמְאֹ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And I will make my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly exceedingly.
pieces: so that I may confirm {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you and greatly increase your descendants."

L.2: and I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly."

R.2: Then I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise to you, and I will give you very many descendants."

decisions.choice: I will make my covenant: grant, confirm
alternatives: I will make a new covenant
decisions.reason: The verb is "give": God gives or confirms the covenant made in chapter 15, now with its sign.

decisions.choice: my, me (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself, so "my" and "me" take the deity pronoun setting throughout the chapter.

records.source: וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַבְרָ֖ם עַל־פָּנָ֑יו וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And fell Abram on his face, and spoke with him God, saying,
pieces: Abram fell face down, and God said to him,

L.3: Then Abram fell on his face, and God spoke with him, saying,

R.3: Abram bowed down with his face to the ground, and God said to him,

decisions.choice: fell on his face: bowed to the ground
decisions.reason: Falling face down is a sign of reverence and submission before God (Leviticus 9:24).

records.source: אֲנִ֕י הִנֵּ֥ה בְרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וְהָיִ֕יתָ לְאַ֖ב הֲמ֥וֹן גּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: I, behold, my covenant [is] with you, and you will become [the] father of a multitude of nations.
pieces: "Here is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you, from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} side: you will become the father of many nations.

L.4: "As for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, look, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant is with you, and you shall be the father of a multitude of nations.

R.4: "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise to you: you will be the father of many nations.

decisions.choice: the father of a multitude of nations: more than one people
decisions.reason: Abraham will be father of Israel, of Ishmael's and Esau's peoples, and of the children of Keturah (25:1-4). Paul reads the promise as fulfilled in all who share Abraham's faith (Romans 4:16-17).

records.source: וְלֹא־יִקָּרֵ֥א ע֛וֹד אֶת־שִׁמְךָ֖ אַבְרָ֑ם וְהָיָ֤ה שִׁמְךָ֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם כִּ֛י אַב־הֲמ֥וֹן גּוֹיִ֖ם נְתַתִּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And not will be called again your name Abram, and will be your name Abraham, for [the] father of a multitude of nations I have made you.
pieces: Your name will no longer be Abram. From now on it is Abraham, since I have made you a father of many nations.

L.5: No longer shall your name be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.

R.5: Your name will not be Abram anymore. It will be Abraham, because I have made you the father of many nations.

decisions.choice: Abram ... Abraham: "exalted father" ... "father of a multitude"
decisions.reason: Abram means "exalted father". Abraham is explained by its sound: av hamon, "father of a multitude". A new name marks a new calling, given by God (32:28).

decisions.choice: I have made you: as good as done
decisions.reason: The completed form announces God's promise as already settled, though Abraham has as yet one son.

records.source: וְהִפְרֵתִ֤י אֹֽתְךָ֙ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד וּנְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְגוֹיִ֑ם וּמְלָכִ֖ים מִמְּךָ֥ יֵצֵֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And I will make you fruitful exceedingly exceedingly, and I will make you into nations, and kings from you will come out.
pieces: I will make you abundantly fruitful; nations will come from you, and kings will be among your descendants.

L.6: I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come from you.

R.6: I will give you many, many descendants. They will become nations, and some of them will be kings.

decisions.choice: kings shall come from you: the kings of Israel
decisions.reason: The promise of kings looks ahead to Israel's kings, above all David (2 Samuel 7:12).

records.source: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֨י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֜י בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֗ךָ וּבֵ֨ין זַרְעֲךָ֧ אַחֲרֶ֛יךָ לְדֹרֹתָ֖ם לִבְרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֑ם לִהְי֤וֹת לְךָ֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֖ אַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And I will establish my covenant between me and you and your offspring after you for their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be to you God and to your offspring after you.
pieces: I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you and your descendants after you for generations to come, as an everlasting covenant: I will be your God and the God of your descendants after you.

L.7: And I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations, an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your offspring after you.

R.7: My promise to you and your descendants will last forever. I will be your God, and the God of all your descendants after you.

decisions.choice: to be God to you and to your offspring: the heart of the covenant
decisions.reason: The promise "I will be your God" is the center of every covenant God makes with his people (Exodus 6:7; Jeremiah 31:33; Revelation 21:3).

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֣י לְ֠ךָ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ֨ אַחֲרֶ֜יךָ אֵ֣ת׀אֶ֣רֶץ מְגֻרֶ֗יךָ אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן לַאֲחֻזַּ֖ת עוֹלָ֑ם וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I will give to you and to your offspring after you [the] land of your sojournings, all [the] land of Canaan, for a possession everlasting; and I will be to them God.
pieces: I will give you and your descendants after you all the land of Canaan, the land where you are now a foreigner, to hold for all time, and I will be their God."

L.8: And I will give to you and to your offspring after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession; and I will be their God."

R.8: I will give you and your descendants all the land of Canaan, where you are now living as a stranger. It will be theirs forever, and I will be their God."

decisions.choice: the land of your sojournings: the land where you live as a foreigner
decisions.reason: Abraham lives in Canaan as a resident foreigner (12:10; 23:4). The land he owns none of is promised to his descendants.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֔ם וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֣י תִשְׁמֹ֑ר אַתָּ֛ה וְזַרְעֲךָ֥ אַֽחֲרֶ֖יךָ לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said God to Abraham, and you, my covenant you will keep, you and your offspring after you for their generations.
pieces: God also said to Abraham, "Your part is to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, you and your descendants after you in every generation.

L.9: And God said to Abraham, "As for you, you shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, you and your offspring after you throughout their generations.

R.9: Then God said to Abraham, "You and your descendants after you must keep your part of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise for all time.

decisions.choice: as for you, you shall keep my covenant: Abraham's part
decisions.reason: After "as for me" (verse 4) comes "as for you": the covenant has an obligation on Abraham's side, the keeping of its sign.

records.source: זֹ֣את בְּרִיתִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁמְר֗וּ בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ הִמּ֥וֹל לָכֶ֖ם כָּל־זָכָֽר׃
records.gloss: This [is] my covenant which you will keep between me and you and your offspring after you: will be circumcised to you every male.
pieces: Here is the covenant you and your descendants are to keep with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: every male among you is to be circumcised.

L.10: This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, which you shall keep, between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you and your offspring after you: every male among you shall be circumcised.

R.10: This is what you must do to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise: every boy and man among you must be circumcised.

decisions.choice: circumcised: the cutting away of the foreskin
decisions.reason: Circumcision was practiced by other peoples of the region, but here it is given a new meaning: the sign of belonging to God's covenant people.

records.source: וּנְמַלְתֶּ֕ם אֵ֖ת בְּשַׂ֣ר עָרְלַתְכֶ֑ם וְהָיָה֙ לְא֣וֹת בְּרִ֔ית בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵינֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will be circumcised [in] the flesh of your foreskin, and it will be a sign of [the] covenant between me and you.
pieces: You are to cut away the flesh of your foreskin, and it will be the sign of the covenant between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you.

L.11: You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskins, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you.

R.11: You must cut off the foreskin of your bodies. This will show that you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and that I have made this promise to you.

decisions.choice: a sign of the covenant: as the rainbow was for Noah
decisions.reason: As the bow was the sign of the covenant with Noah (9:12-17), circumcision is the sign of the covenant with Abraham, carried in the body. Later scripture calls for circumcision of the heart as well (Deuteronomy 10:16; Romans 2:28-29).

records.source: וּבֶן־שְׁמֹנַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים יִמּ֥וֹל לָכֶ֛ם כָּל־זָכָ֖ר לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֑ם יְלִ֣יד בָּ֔יִת וּמִקְנַת־כֶּ֨סֶף֙ מִכֹּ֣ל בֶּן־נֵכָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹ֥א מִֽזַּרְעֲךָ֖ הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And a son of eight days will be circumcised to you, every male, for your generations, one born in [the] house and one bought with silver from any foreigner, who [is] not of your offspring.
pieces: Every male among you who is eight days old must be circumcised, generation after generation, including slaves born in your household or bought with money from a foreigner who is not one of your descendants.

L.12: At eight days old every male among you shall be circumcised, throughout your generations, whether born in your household or bought with silver from any foreigner who is not of your offspring.

R.12: From now on, every baby boy must be circumcised when he is eight days old. This includes the boys and men who are slaves in your household, whether they were born there or bought from foreigners.

decisions.choice: eight days old: the set time for circumcision
decisions.reason: The rule is kept in the law of Moses (Leviticus 12:3) and in the New Testament (Luke 1:59; 2:21).

decisions.choice: born in the household or bought: the covenant includes the whole household
decisions.reason: Slaves of the household, foreigners by birth, receive the sign too. Belonging to the covenant was never only a matter of descent.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" in Readable and Balanced, as the style guide keeps it for people bought with money (m2).

records.source: הִמּ֧וֹל׀יִמּ֛וֹל יְלִ֥יד בֵּֽיתְךָ֖ וּמִקְנַ֣ת כַּסְפֶּ֑ךָ וְהָיְתָ֧ה בְרִיתִ֛י בִּבְשַׂרְכֶ֖ם לִבְרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: Being circumcised he will be circumcised, [the one] born in your house and [the one] bought with your silver; and will be my covenant in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
pieces: Every one of them, whether born in your household or bought with your money, must be circumcised. So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant will be in your flesh, a covenant for all time.

L.13: He who is born in your household and he who is bought with your silver must surely be circumcised; so shall {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant be in your flesh, an everlasting covenant.

R.13: All of them must be circumcised, both those born in your household and those you buy. This will be the sign in your bodies that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise lasts forever.

decisions.choice: surely be circumcised: the doubled verb makes the command firm
decisions.reason: As in 2:17, repeating the verb gives it emphasis: this is not optional.

records.source: וְעָרֵ֣ל׀זָכָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יִמּוֹל֙ אֶת־בְּשַׂ֣ר עָרְלָת֔וֹ וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵעַמֶּ֑יהָ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖י הֵפַֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And an uncircumcised male who is not circumcised [in] the flesh of his foreskin, will be cut off that person from his people; my covenant he has broken.
pieces: A male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin is to be cut off from his people. He has broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant."

L.14: Any uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin shall be cut off from his people; he has broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant."

R.14: Any male who is not circumcised will no longer belong to my people, because he has broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise."

decisions.choice: cut off from his people: excluded from the covenant community
decisions.reason: "Cut off" may mean excluded from the people, or death by God's hand; the phrase recurs in the law (Exodus 12:15). There is a wordplay: a man who refuses to be cut (circumcised) will be cut off.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֔ם שָׂרַ֣י אִשְׁתְּךָ֔ לֹא־תִקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמָ֖הּ שָׂרָ֑י כִּ֥י שָׂרָ֖ה שְׁמָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And said God to Abraham, Sarai your wife, not you will call her name Sarai, for Sarah [is] her name.
pieces: God said further to Abraham, "Your wife is not to be called Sarai any more. Sarah is her name.

L.15: And God said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name.

R.15: God also said to Abraham, "Do not call your wife Sarai anymore. Her name is now Sarah.

decisions.choice: Sarai ... Sarah: both mean "princess"
decisions.reason: Both forms mean "princess"; Sarah is the newer form. As with Abraham, God gives the new name, and she will be mother of kings (verse 16).

records.heading: A son promised through Sarah

records.source: וּבֵרַכְתִּ֣י אֹתָ֔הּ וְגַ֨ם נָתַ֧תִּי מִמֶּ֛נָּה לְךָ֖ בֵּ֑ן וּבֵֽרַכְתִּ֨יהָ֙ וְהָֽיְתָ֣ה לְגוֹיִ֔ם מַלְכֵ֥י עַמִּ֖ים מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And I will bless her, and also I will give from her to you a son; and I will bless her, and she will become nations; kings of peoples from her will be.
pieces: I will bless her and give you a son through her as well. I will bless her, and nations will come from her; kings of peoples will be among her descendants."

L.16: And I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she shall become nations; kings of peoples shall come from her."

R.16: I will bless her, and she will give you a son. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations. Kings will come from her family."

decisions.choice: I will give you a son by her: the promised son will be Sarah's
decisions.reason: For the first time God says plainly that the son of the promise will be born to Sarah, not to Hagar.

records.source: וַיִּפֹּ֧ל אַבְרָהָ֛ם עַל־פָּנָ֖יו וַיִּצְחָ֑ק וַיֹּ֣אמֶר בְּלִבּ֗וֹ הַלְּבֶ֤ן מֵאָֽה־שָׁנָה֙ יִוָּלֵ֔ד וְאִ֨ם־שָׂרָ֔ה הֲבַת־תִּשְׁעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה תֵּלֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And fell Abraham on his face and laughed and said in his heart, to a son of a hundred years will [one] be born, and Sarah, a daughter of ninety years, will she bear?
pieces: Abraham bowed face down, but he laughed and said to himself, "Can a man a hundred years old become a father? Can Sarah have a baby at ninety?"

L.17: Then Abraham fell on his face and laughed and said in his heart, "Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? And shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?"

R.17: Abraham bowed down with his face to the ground. But he laughed and thought, "How can a man who is a hundred years old have a child? How can Sarah have a baby when she is ninety?"

decisions.choice: laughed: the root of Isaac's name
decisions.reason: The verb (yitschaq) is the name Isaac (Yitschaq). Abraham's laugh, part wonder, part disbelief, is remembered in his son's name (verse 19; 18:12; 21:6).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶל־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים ל֥וּ יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל יִחְיֶ֥ה לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Abraham to God, if only Ishmael would live before you!
pieces: And Abraham said to God, "Oh, let Ishmael be the one who lives in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor!"

L.18: And Abraham said to God, "Oh that Ishmael might live before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

R.18: Abraham said to God, "Please let Ishmael be the one to receive {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blessing!"

decisions.choice: might live before you: live under your favor
decisions.reason: Abraham asks that Ishmael, the son he already has, may enjoy God's favor and carry the promise.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲבָל֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֗ יֹלֶ֤דֶת לְךָ֙ בֵּ֔ן וְקָרָ֥אתָ אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ יִצְחָ֑ק וַהֲקִמֹתִ֨י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֥י אִתּ֛וֹ לִבְרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם לְזַרְע֥וֹ אַחֲרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said God, no, Sarah your wife [will be] bearing to you a son, and you will call his name Isaac; and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.
pieces: God replied, "No. Your wife Sarah will have a son by you, and you will name him Isaac. With him I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, a covenant for all time with his descendants after him.

L.19: And God said, "No, but Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac. I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.

R.19: But God said, "No, your wife Sarah will have a son, and you must name him Isaac. I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} promise to him and to his descendants after him forever.

decisions.choice: Isaac: "he laughs"
decisions.reason: The name means "he laughs", recalling Abraham's laughter (verse 17).

decisions.choice: no, but: a firm correction
decisions.reason: The word (aval) corrects Abraham's suggestion: the covenant son will be Sarah's.

records.source: וּֽלְיִשְׁמָעֵ֘אלשְׁמַעְתִּיךָ֒ הִנֵּ֣ה׀בֵּרַ֣כְתִּי אֹת֗וֹ וְהִפְרֵיתִ֥י אֹת֛וֹ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֥י אֹת֖וֹ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֤ר נְשִׂיאִם֙ יוֹלִ֔יד וּנְתַתִּ֖יו לְג֥וֹי גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And as for Ishmael, I have heard you; behold, I will bless him and make him fruitful and multiply him exceedingly exceedingly; twelve princes he will father, and I will make him a great nation.
pieces: I have heard your prayer for Ishmael too. I will bless him, give him many children and multiply his descendants greatly. He will be the father of twelve chieftains, and I will make a great nation of him.

L.20: And as for Ishmael, I have heard you: look, I will bless him and make him fruitful and multiply him exceedingly. He shall father twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.

R.20: And I have heard what you asked about Ishmael. I will bless him too. I will give him many descendants. He will be the father of twelve leaders, and his descendants will become a great nation.

decisions.choice: I have heard you: a play on Ishmael's name
decisions.reason: "I have heard" (shema'tikha) echoes the name Ishmael, "God hears" (16:11).

decisions.choice: twelve princes: the tribes of Ishmael
decisions.reason: The twelve are named in 25:13-16, a counterpart to the twelve tribes of Israel.

records.source: וְאֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖י אָקִ֣ים אֶת־יִצְחָ֑ק אֲשֶׁר֩ תֵּלֵ֨ד לְךָ֤ שָׂרָה֙ לַמּוֹעֵ֣ד הַזֶּ֔ה בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הָאַחֶֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: And my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom will bear to you Sarah at this appointed time in the next year.
pieces: But it is with Isaac, the son Sarah will bear you about this time next year, that I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant."

L.21: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this set time next year."

R.21: But I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} special promise with Isaac. Sarah will give birth to him at this time next year."

records.source: וַיְכַ֖ל לְדַבֵּ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וַיַּ֣עַל אֱלֹהִ֔ים מֵעַ֖ל אַבְרָהָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he finished speaking with him, and went up God from Abraham.
pieces: When God had finished speaking with Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up and left him.

L.22: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had finished speaking with him, God went up from Abraham.

R.22: When God finished talking with Abraham, God went up and left him.

decisions.choice: God went up: the end of the appearance
decisions.reason: As God appeared (verse 1), so he leaves (35:13). The text does not describe the appearance itself.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בְּנ֗וֹ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־יְלִידֵ֤י בֵיתוֹ֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־מִקְנַ֣ת כַּסְפּ֔וֹ כָּל־זָכָ֕ר בְּאַנְשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֣ית אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיָּ֜מָל אֶת־בְּשַׂ֣ר עָרְלָתָ֗ם בְּעֶ֨צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And took Abraham Ishmael his son and all those born in his house and all those bought with his silver, every male among the men of [the] house of Abraham, and circumcised [the] flesh of their foreskin on that very day, as had spoken with him God.
pieces: Abraham did it the same day. He took his son Ishmael and every male of his household, whether born there or bought with his money, and circumcised them, as God had told him.

L.23: Then Abraham took Ishmael his son and all those born in his household and all those bought with his silver, every male among the men of Abraham's household, and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very day, as God had said to him.

R.23: That same day Abraham circumcised his son Ishmael and all the other males in his household, both those born there and those he had bought, just as God had told him.

decisions.choice: that very day: immediate obedience
decisions.reason: Abraham obeys at once, as he did when God first called him (12:4).

records.source: וְאַ֨בְרָהָ֔ם בֶּן־תִּשְׁעִ֥ים וָתֵ֖שַׁע שָׁנָ֑ה בְּהִמֹּל֖וֹ בְּשַׂ֥ר עָרְלָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And Abraham [was] a son of ninety and nine years when he was circumcised [in] the flesh of his foreskin.
pieces: Abraham was ninety-nine when the flesh of his foreskin was cut away,

L.24: Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

R.24: Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised.

records.source: וְיִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בְּנ֔וֹ בֶּן־שְׁלֹ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה בְּהִ֨מֹּל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת בְּשַׂ֥ר עָרְלָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And Ishmael his son [was] a son of thirteen years when he was circumcised [in] the flesh of his foreskin.
pieces: and his son Ishmael was thirteen when he was circumcised.

L.25: And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

R.25: His son Ishmael was thirteen years old when he was circumcised.

records.source: בְּעֶ֨צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה נִמּ֖וֹל אַבְרָהָ֑ם וְיִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל בְּנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: On that very day was circumcised Abraham and Ishmael his son.
pieces: So Abraham and Ishmael were circumcised together that very day,

L.26: On that very day Abraham and Ishmael his son were circumcised.

R.26: Abraham and Ishmael were circumcised on the same day.

records.source: וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֤י בֵיתוֹ֙ יְלִ֣יד בָּ֔יִת וּמִקְנַת־כֶּ֖סֶף מֵאֵ֣ת בֶּן־נֵכָ֑ר נִמֹּ֖לוּ אִתּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And all [the] men of his house, born in [the] house and bought with silver from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
pieces: together with all the men of his household, the slaves born in his house and those bought from foreigners.

L.27: And all the men of his household, those born in the household and those bought with silver from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.

R.27: All the men of his household were circumcised with him, those born in his household and those he had bought from foreigners.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" in Balanced, as the style guide keeps it for people bought with money (verse 12).
